# pidginhost_server_snapshot (Resource)

A snapshot of a cloud server. The API takes snapshots only while the server is active and not booted from an ISO. Every argument is fixed at creation: changing one replaces the snapshot. The API queues snapshot operations, so Terraform follows them in the server's activity log: it fails when the server refuses the operation, and sends it again every 30 seconds while another operation holds the server. Snapshots stay in state until deletion finishes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pidginhost_server_snapshot" "before_upgrade" {
  server_id   = pidginhost_server.web.id
  name        = "before-upgrade"
  description = "Taken before the OS upgrade"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Snapshot name, unique on the server: 2 to 40 letters, digits, _ or -, starting with a letter.
- `server_id` (String) Id of the server.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free text description, up to 200 characters.
- `include_memory` (Boolean) Whether to save the memory of the running server as well. Defaults to false.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the snapshot was taken.
- `id` (String) Server id and snapshot name, as <server_id>/<name>.
- `is_current` (Boolean) Whether this is the server's current snapshot.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a snapshot by server id and snapshot name.
terraform import pidginhost_server_snapshot.before_upgrade 123/before-upgrade
```
